recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for core. Future Permission rule-logic work should be made in HL7/data-access-policies unless a later final work group decision moves Permission back into the active core build.
issue_request: Applied/Persuasive Security issue for R6 asking to clarify Permission rule processing: repeated Permission.rule.data and Permission.rule.activity instances are OR alternatives, elements and repetitions within each data/activity repetition are AND conditions, Permission.rule.data.period should be 0..1, and examples should be placed into element comments.
initial_application: Jira's application comment points to HL7/fhir merge commit 2268c17c01881bb6256b9c2a61c98afd75396e98 / PR #3054. That commit added Permission rules-processing narrative, added StructureDefinition comments for rule/data/activity/limit, and changed Permission.rule.data.period from 0..* to 0..1 while Permission was still active in core.
additional_context: Later core commit 0e2a8a7f839d5e1a43787523daccf07d958362f3 removed source/permission and active Permission fhir.ini entries. Current core Security/history pages link Permission to the Data Access Policies IG. Security and FMG evidence records the decision to keep Permission out of R6 core as a non-core/additional resource, and HL7/data-access-policies PR #57 moved the Permission source into that IG. Current Data Access Policies source retains the FHIR-44748 comments and period cardinality.
reconciliation: No core source was changed. The correct reconciliation is an empty external-repo audit because reintroducing or editing source/permission in core would conflict with the later move out of core, and the external current source already carries the requested clarification.
